problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=⟨\sqrt{4-t},\,{t}^{2}-1,\,(t-2)^{3}⟩.$

feedback.problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}t \\ \sqrt{2t+4} \\ {t}^{4}-{t}^{3}\end{aligned}].$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f,$ we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components. 

- The domain of $t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of $\sqrt{2t+4}$ is $t\in [-2,\infty ).$

- The domain of ${t}^{4}-{t}^{3}$ is  $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14033854/assets/d0819fe7e3b82bbf46f6118145903e4dc5640acca4fedf66a734b4d37466e368.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is $t\in [-2,\infty ).$
